claim: Bacterial biofilms are communities of bacteria usually attached to solid strata and often differentiated into complex structures.
source: Bacterial biofilms are communities of bacteria usually attached to solid strata and often differentiated into complex structures.
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by established scientific knowledge about biofilms.

claim: Communication across biofilms has been shown to involve chemical signaling.
source: Communication across biofilms has been shown to involve chemical signaling and, more recently, electrical signaling in Gram-positive biofilms.
evidence: This statement references established scientific knowledge about biofilm communication mechanisms.

claim: Electrical signaling has been shown to occur in Gram-positive biofilms.
source: Communication across biofilms has been shown to involve chemical signaling and, more recently, electrical signaling in Gram-positive biofilms.
evidence: This statement references established scientific knowledge about electrical signaling in Gram-positive biofilms.

claim: Community-level synchronized membrane potential dynamics occur in three-dimensional Escherichia coli biofilms.
source: We report for the first time, community-level synchronized membrane potential dynamics in three-dimensional Escherichia coli biofilms.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Two hyperpolarization events are observed in E. coli biofilms in response to light stress.
source: Two hyperpolarization events are observed in response to light stress.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The first hyperpolarization event requires mechanically sensitive ion channels (MscK, MscL, and MscS).
source: The first requires mechanically sensitive ion channels (MscK, MscL, and MscS) and the second needs the Kch-potassium channel.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mutant strains lacking these channels.

claim: The second hyperpolarization event needs the Kch-potassium channel.
source: The first requires mechanically sensitive ion channels (MscK, MscL, and MscS) and the second needs the Kch-potassium channel.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Kch deletion mutants.

claim: The ion channels mediate both local spiking of single E. coli biofilms and long-range coordinated electrical signaling in E. coli biofilms.
source: The channels mediated both local spiking of single E. coli biofilms and long-range coordinated electrical signaling in E. coli biofilms.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations at both single cell and biofilm levels.

claim: The electrical phenomena are explained using Hodgkin-Huxley and 3D fire-diffuse-fire agent-based models.
source: The electrical phenomena are explained using Hodgkin-Huxley and 3D fire-diffuse-fire agent-based models.
evidence: The manuscript presents these models and shows their agreement with experimental data.

claim: Electrical wavefronts based on potassium ions are a mechanism by which signaling occurs in Gram-negative biofilms.
source: These data demonstrate that electrical wavefronts based on potassium ions are a mechanism by which signaling occurs in Gram-negative biofilms and as such may represent a conserved mechanism for communication across biofilms.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing potassium ion changes and electrical signaling.

claim: Electrical wavefronts based on potassium ions may represent a conserved mechanism for communication across biofilms.
source: These data demonstrate that electrical wavefronts based on potassium ions are a mechanism by which signaling occurs in Gram-negative biofilms and as such may represent a conserved mechanism for communication across biofilms.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the similarity to Gram-positive biofilms.

claim: Biofilms account for approximately 80% of chronic infections.
source: Biofilms account for ~80% of chronic infections and are costly to eradicate in medical applications (Sharma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sharma et al., 2016.

claim: Biofilms are costly to eradicate in medical applications.
source: Biofilms account for ~80% of chronic infections and are costly to eradicate in medical applications (Sharma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sharma et al., 2016.

claim: Bacteria in biofilms have recently been found to modulate their membrane potentials similar to excitable eukaryotic cells.
source: Bacteria in biofilms have recently been found to modulate their membrane potentials similar to excitable eukaryotic cells (Liu et al., 2017; Whitehead et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2017 and Whitehead et al., 2001.

claim: Potassium ion-channel-linked electrical signaling was first characterized in Gram-positive Bacillus subtilis biofilms.
source: Potassium ion-channel-linked electrical signaling was first characterized in Gram-positive Bacillus subtilis biofilms (Prindle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Prindle et al., 2015.

claim: Potassium ion-channel-linked electrical signaling enables communication in bacterial biofilms due to the transmission of potassium wavefronts in the local environment of the biofilm.
source: It enables communication in bacterial biofilms due to the transmission of potassium wavefronts in the local environment of the biofilm.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from previous studies on B. subtilis.

claim: The potassium wavefront occurs in both centripetal and centrifugal varieties.
source: The potassium wavefront occurs in both centripetal and centrifugal varieties (Blee et al., 2019) and emerges spontaneously after the biofilm has grown to a critical size (Coombes, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Blee et al., 2019.

claim: The potassium wavefront emerges spontaneously after the biofilm has grown to a critical size.
source: The potassium wavefront occurs in both centripetal and centrifugal varieties (Blee et al., 2019) and emerges spontaneously after the biofilm has grown to a critical size (Coombes, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Coombes, 2001.

claim: Photodynamic therapy using blue light causes a process of stage-dependent cell dispersal in biofilms and membrane hyperpolarization.
source: Photodynamic therapy using blue light causes a process of stage-dependent cell dispersal in biofilms and membrane hyperpolarization (Blee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Blee et al., 2020.

claim: Blue light therapy has been investigated in detail for the treatment of topical infections.
source: Such therapy has thus been investigated in detail for the treatment of topical infections (Kharkwal et al., 2011; Cieplik et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kharkwal et al., 2011 and Cieplik et al., 2018.

claim: Membrane potential dynamics in prokaryotes are orchestrated using ion-channels.
source: Membrane potential dynamics in prokaryotes are orchestrated using ion-channels.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about prokaryotic physiology.

claim: Gating of ion channels can be controlled by voltage changes, heat, light stress, metabolic stress, mechanical stress, and chemical agents.
source: Gating of these channels can be controlled by voltage changes, heat, light stress, metabolic stress, mechanical stress, and chemical agents (Prindle et al., 2015; Bruni et al., 2017; Martinac et al., 2008; MacKinnon, 2004; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In B. subtilis biofilms, only the potassium ion channel, YugO, has been directly linked to electrical signaling.
source: In B. subtilis biofilms, only the potassium ion channel, YugO, has been directly linked to electrical signaling (Prindle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Prindle et al., 2015.

claim: Robust ion-channel-mediated signaling in biofilms of Gram-negative bacteria has not been described to date.
source: To date, robust ion-channel-mediated signaling in biofilms of Gram-negative bacteria has not been described.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature prior to this study.

claim: Gram-negative bacterial biofilms have higher resistance to antimicrobial molecules than Gram-positive bacterial biofilms.
source: Gram-negative bacterial biofilms have higher resistance to antimicrobial molecules than Gram-positive bacterial biofilms (Mishra et al., 2020; Bruni and Kralj, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mishra et al., 2020 and Bruni and Kralj, 2020.

claim: Voltage-related spiking dynamics have been observed in single E. coli cells.
source: Although voltage-related spiking dynamics have been observed in single E. coli cells (Bruni and Kralj, 2020; Kralj et al., 2011), only second long stochastic transients have been measured with no distinct coordination between intercellular spikes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bruni and Kralj, 2020 and Kralj et al., 2011.

claim: Only second long stochastic transients have been measured in single E. coli cells with no distinct coordination between intercellular spikes.
source: Although voltage-related spiking dynamics have been observed in single E. coli cells (Bruni and Kralj, 2020; Kralj et al., 2011), only second long stochastic transients have been measured with no distinct coordination between intercellular spikes.
evidence: This is a statement about previous observations in the literature.

claim: The Kch potassium ion channel in E. coli was discovered by Milkman, 1994 using comparative genetic techniques.
source: The Kch potassium ion channel in E. coli was discovered in E. coli by Milkman, 1994 using comparative genetic techniques.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Milkman, 1994.

claim: The current consensus is that Kch is a voltage-gated ion channel, although the evidence is slightly indirect.
source: The current consensus is that Kch is a voltage-gated ion channel, although the evidence is slightly indirect (Kuo et al., 2003; Beagle and Lockless, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kuo et al., 2003 and Beagle and Lockless, 2021.

claim: The current study provides additional evidence for the voltage-gated nature of the Kch channel in E. coli.
source: The current study provides additional evidence for the voltage-gated nature of the Kch channel in E. coli and indicates a physiological role for the ion channel.
evidence: This is a claim about the contribution of the current study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: The current study indicates a physiological role for the Kch ion channel.
source: The current study provides additional evidence for the voltage-gated nature of the Kch channel in E. coli and indicates a physiological role for the ion channel.
evidence: This is a claim about the contribution of the current study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Under light stress, E. coli hyperpolarize twice in response to continued light radiation.
source: We found that under light stress, E. coli hyperpolarize twice in response to continued light radiation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The first peak is when E. coli first register the presence of an external stressor in their vicinity and appears to be mediated by mechanosensitive (MS) ion channels.
source: We hypothesize that the first peak is when E. coli first register the presence of an external stressor in their vicinity and appears to be mediated by mechanosensitive (MS) ion channels.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by experimental data from MS channel mutants.

claim: The depolarization and subsequent second peak that occurs in response to continued stimulation corresponds to a habituation phenomenon and is dependent on the Kch potassium-gated channel.
source: The depolarization and subsequent second peak that occurs in response to continued stimulation corresponds to a habituation phenomenon and is dependent on the Kch potassium-gated channel.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Kch mutants and comparison to neuronal habituation.

claim: Single sparse cells are defined as those with no neighboring cells within 10 µm.
source: Single sparse cells are defined as those with no neighboring cells within 10 µm.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.

claim: ThT is a Nernstian voltage indicator which accumulates because bacterial cells have negative potentials.
source: We monitored the membrane potential dynamics with the cationic fluorescent dye, Thioflavin (ThT; Biancalana and Koide, 2010). ThT is a Nernstian voltage indicator Plásek and Sigler, 1996 which accumulates because bacterial cells have negative potentials (Blee et al., 2020; Stratford et al., 2019; Humphries et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations about ThT properties.

claim: A cell-wide rise in the intensity of fluorescence was observed in single E. coli cells exposed to blue light, followed by a period of quiescence and then a slow increase in intensity which persisted until the end of the 60-min experiments.
source: We observed a cell-wide rise in the intensity of fluorescence, a period of quiescence followed by a slow increase in intensity which persisted until the end of the 60-min experiments (Figure 1B, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: Applying the blue light for different time periods and over different timescales yielded no change in the number of peaks.
source: Applying the blue light for different time periods and over different timescales yielded no change in the number of peaks (Appendix 1—figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1A.

claim: The spike profile existed in other E. coli strains (E. coli BW25113).
source: We confirmed that this spike profile existed in other E. coli strains (E. coli BW25113, Appendix 1—figure 1B) and was also detectable when E. coli cells were grown in Minimal (M9) media (Appendix 1—figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1B.

claim: The spike profile was detectable when E. coli cells were grown in Minimal (M9) media.
source: We confirmed that this spike profile existed in other E. coli strains (E. coli BW25113, Appendix 1—figure 1B) and was also detectable when E. coli cells were grown in Minimal (M9) media (Appendix 1—figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1C.

claim: Similar spiking dynamics were observed when the lipophilic cationic cell permeant membrane potential dye, tetramethyl rhodamine methyl ester (TMRM) was employed.
source: We observed similar spiking dynamics when we employed the lipophilic cationic cell permeant membrane potential dye, tetramethyl rhodamine methyl ester (TMRM; Appendix 1—figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1D.

claim: CCCP rapidly quenches membrane potential related dynamics in E. coli.
source: We used carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazone (CCCP) which rapidly quenches membrane potential related dynamics in E. coli (Yang et al., 2020; Kralj et al., 2011; Perry et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2020; Kralj et al., 2011; Perry et al., 2011.

claim: When CCCP was added, a fast efflux of ions in all cells and no spiking dynamics was observed, confirming that the observed dynamics is membrane potential related.
source: When CCCP was added, we observed a fast efflux of ions in all cells and no spiking dynamics (Appendix 1—figure 1E), confirming that the observed dynamics is membrane potential related.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1E.

claim: A microcluster is defined as a cell community in which intercellular distances do not exceed two cellular diameters.
source: A microcluster is defined as a cell community in which intercellular distances do not exceed two cellular diameters (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.

claim: The average time-to-first peak was 7.34 ± 10.89 ± 4.44 min (mean ± SD ± SE) for sparse cells and 3.24 ± 1.77 ± 0.53 min (mean ± SD ± SE) for microclustered cells.
source: The analysis of time-to-first peak latencies in sparse and microclustered cells showed that the average time-to-first peak was 7.34 ± 10.89 ± 4.44 min (mean ± SD ± SE) and 3.24 ± 1.77 ± 0.53 min (mean ± SD ± SE; Figure 1E), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The membrane potential dynamics of single cells showed more variability in spikes and less synchrony in the phases of the first spikes than those in microclusters.
source: The membrane potential dynamics of single cells showed more variability in spikes and less synchrony in the phases of the first spikes than those in microclusters (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and D.

claim: Random electrical signaling in E. coli synchronizes as the cells become clustered.
source: This suggests that random electrical signaling in E. coli synchronizes as the cells become clustered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences between sparse and clustered cells.

claim: 10 µM of ThT does not affect the growth of the E. coli strains used in the experiment.
source: We also confirmed that 10 µM of ThT does not affect the growth of the E. coli strains used in the experiment (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A spontaneous rapid rise in spikes within cells in the center of the biofilm was observed while cells at the periphery remained significantly less bright when mature biofilm was exposed to blue light.
source: We observed a spontaneous rapid rise in spikes within cells in the center of the biofilm while cells at the periphery remained significantly less bright (Figure 2A and B, Video 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Video 3.

claim: The ion-channel-mediated wavefronts moved from the center of the biofilm to the edges.
source: The ion-channel-mediated wavefronts moved from the center of the biofilm to the edges.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations of wavefront propagation.

claim: The wavefronts rapidly collapsed from the edges to the center of the biofilm.
source: The wavefronts then rapidly collapsed from the edges to the center of the biofilm.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations of wavefront propagation.

claim: Once the wavefront reached the center, the whole system engaged in a period of quiescence and remained dark even in the presence of the continued external light stimulation.
source: Once the wavefront reached the center, the whole system engaged in a period of quiescence and remained dark even in the presence of the continued external light stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: After a few minutes of inactivity, the wavefront reemerged from the center of the biofilm and slowly reached the periphery of the biofilm.
source: After a few minutes of inactivity, the wavefront reemerged from the center of the biofilm and slowly reached the periphery of the biofilm.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: After reaching the edges for the second time, the hyperpolarization persisted, and the entire biofilm remained bright and showed no noticeable change in response to the continued presence of the external stimuli.
source: After reaching the edges for the second time, the hyperpolarization persisted, and the entire biofilm remained bright and showed no noticeable change in response to the continued presence of the external stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: The latency of the first peak in biofilms was 2.73 ± 0.85 ± 0.15 min (mean ± SD ± SE).
source: The latency of the first peak was 2.73 ± 0.85 ± 0.15 min (mean ± SD ± SE).
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements.

claim: The latency of the first peak in biofilms was much smaller than that of cells in microclusters and sparse cells.
source: This was a much smaller period than that of cells in microclusters and sparse cells (Figure 1B and D, Appendix 1—figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental data.

claim: The variability of the latency (SD) in biofilms was much lower than in microclusters and sparse cells.
source: Furthermore, the variability of the latency (SD) was much lower.
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements.

claim: Similar intensity profiles were observed for all biofilms of different shapes and sizes.
source: Biofilms of different shapes and sizes were grown and we observed similar intensity profiles for all the biofilms (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The amplitude of the action potentials does not depend on biofilm density or areal coverage of the biofilm.
source: The peaks of the spiking profiles in all the biofilms (Figure 2C) show that the amplitude of the action potentials does not depend on biofilm density or areal coverage of the biofilm.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The wavefront dynamics is robust once the biofilm has an appreciable size.
source: The intensity profile of different biofilms across several experiments shows that the wavefront dynamics is robust once the biofilm has an appreciable size (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Coordinated signaling directs ion-channel-mediated wavefronts in E. coli biofilms.
source: These data provide evidence that coordinated signaling directs ion-channel-mediated wavefronts in E. coli biofilms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed synchronized wavefront dynamics.

claim: E. coli biofilms use electrical signaling to coordinate long-range responses to light stress.
source: This data suggests that E. coli biofilms use electrical signaling to coordinate long-range responses to light stress.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed wavefront propagation.

claim: The Kch ion channel helps E. coli to survive environmental stress.
source: This ion channel (Figure 3A) helps E. coli to survive environmental stress (Loukin et al., 2005), but its deletion does not impede the development of E. coli from single cells into biofilms (Loukin et al., 2005; Kuo et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Loukin et al., 2005.

claim: Deletion of Kch does not impede the development of E. coli from single cells into biofilms.
source: This ion channel (Figure 3A) helps E. coli to survive environmental stress (Loukin et al., 2005), but its deletion does not impede the development of E. coli from single cells into biofilms (Loukin et al., 2005; Kuo et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Loukin et al., 2005 and Kuo et al., 2005.

claim: Kch had not been previously linked to action potentials and electrical signaling in E. coli biofilms.
source: Kch had not been previously linked to action potentials and electrical signaling in E. coli biofilms (Kuo et al., 2003; Beagle and Lockless, 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature prior to this study.

claim: Deletion of Kch inactivates the second peak in single cell E. coli DH5α.
source: We applied light stimulation to a ∆kch mutant of strain BW25113 from the Keio collection Baba et al., 2006 and saw a fast burst of membrane hyperpolarization identical to the wild-type, but there was a plateau that remained for the whole duration of the experiment (Appendix 1—figure 3C, Video 4). There was no repolarization or slow rise to the second peak seen in the wildtype (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The K+ ion channel Kch plays a role in the refractoriness and habituation of the dynamics but does not control the initial hyperpolarization event.
source: This suggests that the K+ ion channel Kch plays a role in the refractoriness and habituation of the dynamics but does not control the initial hyperpolarization event.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotype of Kch deletion mutants.

claim: Kch potassium ion channels are important for electrical signaling in E. coli in the presence of blue light stress.
source: These data showed that Kch potassium ion channels are important for electrical signaling in E. coli in the presence of blue light stress.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Kch mutants.

claim: The kch complemented strain displayed the same membrane potential dynamics observed in the wildtype.
source: To validate the importance of the Kch channel in the membrane potential dynamics of E. coli, we complemented the kch mutation by introducing a plasmid that carries a cloned functional kch gene into strain ∆kch-DH5α. The kch complemented strain displayed the same membrane potential dynamics (Appendix 1—figure 3D) observed in the wildtype (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 3D.

claim: The quiescence period in the kch complemented strain was reduced compared with the wildtype, presumably due to an increased degree of expression of the kch gene on a multi-copy plasmid.
source: However, the quiescence period in our kch complemented strain was reduced compared with the wildtype, presumably due to an increased degree of expression of the kch gene on a multi-copy plasmid.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed phenotype and knowledge of plasmid expression.

claim: For all irradiances tested, a first peak in the ThT fluorescence was observed.
source: For all the irradiances, we observed a first peak in the ThT fluorescence (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The time to the first peak decreased as the light irradiance was increased.
source: The time to the first peak decreased as the light irradiance was increased (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The fast burst of hyperpolarization and repolarization only occurred above the threshold of 15.99 µW/mm2.
source: The fast burst of hyperpolarization and repolarization only occurred above the threshold of 15.99 µW/mm2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on irradiance effects.

claim: For irradiances above the threshold, the dynamics exhibited progressively faster hyperpolarization to the second peak with increased light.
source: For irradiances above this threshold, the dynamics exhibited progressively faster hyperpolarization to the second peak with increased light, which was not observed for irradiances below the threshold.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on irradiance effects.

claim: A sharp rise, a quiescence period and then a plateau similar to that of the ThT dynamics was observed for extracellular potassium ion changes.
source: We thereafter examined the extracellular changes in the potassium ion, K+ ions, within regions close to biofilms. We used the yellow-green fluorescent potassium (K+) indicator, ION potassium Green-4 (IPG-4), which can track changes in extracellular concentrations of potassium. We observed a sharp rise, a quiescence period and then a plateau similar to that of the ThT dynamics (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: K+ ions play a vital role in the observed membrane potential dynamics of the biofilm.
source: This suggests that K+ ions play a vital role in the observed membrane potential dynamics of the biofilm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between potassium changes and membrane potential dynamics.

claim: 1.7% of DH5α cells stained red with propidium iodide after 60 min of light exposure.
source: Damaged cells appear red and we observed that 1.7% of cells stained red after 60 min of light exposure for the DH5α Figure 4D (1) and 7.6% for the DH5α ∆kch mutant (Figure 4D) (2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 7.6% of DH5α ∆kch mutant cells stained red with propidium iodide after 60 min of light exposure.
source: Damaged cells appear red and we observed that 1.7% of cells stained red after 60 min of light exposure for the DH5α Figure 4D (1) and 7.6% for the DH5α ∆kch mutant (Figure 4D) (2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Blue light stress damage to the kch-mutant is significant when compared with the DH5α.
source: Student t-test showed that blue light stress damage to the kch-mutant is significant when compared with the DH5α (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Wildtype DH5α cells which engage in full membrane potential dynamics better withstand the light stress and have lower lethal damage.
source: This data shows that wildtype DH5α cells which engage in full membrane potential dynamics better withstand the light stress and have lower lethal damage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the LiveDead assay results.

claim: After the addition of catalase, cells only registered the presence of the light (via the first peak), but aborted the process of repolarization, so the second hyperpolarization event does not occur.
source: We used the ROS scavenger, catalase, to accelerate the removal of ROS. After the addition of the catalase, cells only registered the presence of the light (via the first peak), but aborted the process of repolarization, so the second hyperpolarization event does not occur (Figure 4F, Video 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and Video 5.

claim: The ion-channel-mediated membrane potential dynamics is a light stress relief process.
source: This demonstrates that the ion-channel-mediated membrane potential dynamics is a light stress relief process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the catalase experiment results.

claim: E. coli manages light stress through well-controlled modulation of its membrane potential dynamics.
source: Our data provide evidence that E. coli manages light stress through well-controlled modulation of its membrane potential dynamics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The light-induced ion-channel-mediated dynamics present at the single cell level become more coordinated at the biofilm level.
source: The light-induced ion-channel-mediated dynamics present at the single cell level become more coordinated at the biofilm level (Videos 1 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental data from single cells and biofilms.

claim: The Hodgkin-Huxley conductance model predicts that the membrane potential dynamics in E. coli biofilms are due to cooperative signaling between two distinct positively charged ion channels (Q and Kch) whose conductivities are voltage gated.
source: Our Hodgkin-Huxley conductance model predicts that the membrane potential dynamics in E. coli biofilms are due to cooperative signaling between two distinct positively charged ion channels (Q and Kch) whose conductivities are voltage gated.
evidence: This is a prediction from the theoretical model developed in the study.

claim: The dynamics causes a process of long-range electrical communication of light stress in the E. coli biofilm.
source: We propose that the dynamics causes a process of long-range electrical communication of light stress in the E. coli biofilm.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the model and experimental observations.

claim: The source of the photooxidative stress was due to increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the vicinity of cells which gradually builds up as the light stress persists.
source: We also propose that the source of the photooxidative stress was due to increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the vicinity of cells which gradually builds up as the light stress persists.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the catalase experiment and known effects of light.

claim: Ion channel Q activates faster than the Kch channel, but deactivates slower than the Kch channel.
source: We predicted that the ion-channels activate and deactivate differently under the light stress (Figure 5A, B). Ion channel Q activates faster than the Kch channel, but deactivates slower than the Kch channel.
evidence: This is a prediction from the Hodgkin-Huxley model.

claim: While the Q channel activation dynamics is more pronounced for the sharp spike of the first peak, the Kch channel controls its subsequent decay.
source: Hence, while the Q channel activation dynamics is more pronounced for the sharp spike of the first peak, the Kch channel controls its subsequent decay.
evidence: This is a prediction from the Hodgkin-Huxley model.

claim: After the first action potential, the Q channel inactivates and contributes minimally to the dynamics.
source: After the first action potential, the Q channel inactivates and contributes minimally to the dynamics.
evidence: This is a prediction from the Hodgkin-Huxley model.

claim: The Kch ion channel controls the slow refractoriness and plateau which persists for a longer period in the presence of constant light stress.
source: The Kch ion channel then controls the slow refractoriness and plateau which persists for a longer period in the presence of constant light stress (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a prediction from the Hodgkin-Huxley model that is consistent with experimental data.

claim: The two ion-channel electrophysiological model correctly produced the same profile as the experimental data.
source: Our two ion-channel electrophysiological model correctly produced the same profile (Figure 5C) as the experimental data (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data.

claim: The model predicts that the two spikes perform different roles in E. coli: the first spike registers the presence of light stress in the environment, while the second spike modulates the light stress by keeping the cell dynamics robust to the intensity of the external light stress.
source: This model also predicts that the two spikes perform different roles in E. coli. The first spike registers the presence of light stress in the environment, while the second spike modulates the light stress by keeping the cell dynamics robust to the intensity of the external light stress.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model.

claim: The mode of signaling is like a specialized type of electrical signaling in neurons called habituation.
source: This mode of signaling is like a specialized type of electrical signaling in neurons called habituation (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with neuronal signaling patterns.

claim: Sensory neurons can engage in signal habituation to remain unresponsive to an external unwanted signal in the environment and still engage in control of other stimuli.
source: Sensory neurons can engage in signal habituation to remain unresponsive to an external unwanted signal in the environment and still engage in control of other stimuli (Herman, 2013; Avery et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations about neuronal habituation.

claim: The model predicts that the opening of the ion channels creates an increased concentration level of the extracellular ions which subsequently results in the depolarization of neighboring cells.
source: The model also predicts that the opening of the ion channels creates an increased concentration level of the extracellular ions which subsequently results in the depolarization of neighboring cells (Yang et al., 2020; Martinez Corral et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a prediction from the model supported by citations.

claim: The MS ion channels help maintain cell turgidity and are also sensitive to stress-related voltage changes.
source: The MS ion channels help maintain cell turgidity and are also sensitive to stress-related voltage changes (Li et al., 2002; Booth, 2014; Haswell et al., 2011; Martinac et al., 2008; van den Berg et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations about MS channel function.

claim: Mutant strains ∆MscK, ∆MscS, and ∆MscL of E. coli BW25113 exposed to light stimulation showed no spike dynamics typically observed with the wildtype cells.
source: We exposed the mutant strains, ∆MscK, ∆MscS, and ∆MscL of the wildtype, E. coli BW25113 (Figure 6C), to light stimulation and observed no spike dynamics typically observed with the wildtype cells (Figures 1B, D, 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The 3D agent-based fire-diffuse-fire model using BSim produced global membrane potential dynamics that are like the experimental data.
source: We developed a 3D agent-based fire-diffuse-fire model (ABFDF) using BSim (Gorochowski et al., 2012). No analytical solutions are known for the FDF model in 3D, so simulations using agent-based models were needed. In our simulated 3D spherical biofilm (Figure 7A), we observed global membrane potential dynamics (Figure 7B, Video 6) that are like our experimental data (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of simulation results with experimental data.

claim: Curvature affects the motion of the wavefronts.
source: Furthermore, the results confirm that curvature affects the motion of the wavefronts (Nagy Ungvarai et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental results and a citation.

claim: The centripetal wavefronts appear to travel faster than the centrifugal wavefronts.
source: The centripetal wavefronts appear to travel faster than the centrifugal wavefronts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anomalous exponents measured.

claim: The critical size for wave initiation predicted from the ABFDF model was 6.17±1.84 µm.
source: This is reasonably close to the value predicted from our ABFDF model, 6.17±1.84 µm.
evidence: This is calculated from simulation data.

claim: 3D E. coli biofilms need to develop a densely packed biofilm above the critical radius for a robust synchronized ion-channel-mediated wavefront to propagate in the system.
source: 3D E. coli biofilms, therefore, need to develop a densely packed biofilm above the critical radius for a robust synchronized ion-channel-mediated wavefront to propagate in the system.
evidence: This is an inference based on the calculated critical size.

claim: 2D B subtilis biofilms need to grow up to 350 µm for a wavefront to emerge in the system.
source: This contrasts with 2D B subtilis biofilms which need to grow up to 350 µm for a wavefront to emerge in the system (Prindle et al., 2015; Martinez-Corral et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on B. subtilis.

claim: The model predicts the transport properties of the wavefront, the patterns of global excitation and the critical radius for wavefront propagation in biofilms.
source: Therefore, our model predicts the transport properties of the wavefront, the patterns of global excitation and the critical radius for wavefront propagation in biofilms (Table 1).
evidence: This is a summary of the model's predictive capabilities.

claim: A slow decrease of velocity was observed as the wavefront spread from the core towards the periphery that is predicted by the Eikonal approximation.
source: As expected, we observed a slow decrease of velocity as the wavefront spread from the core towards the periphery that is predicted by the Eikonal approximation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations and theoretical predictions.

claim: For the velocity of the wavefront that travels back to the core, a decrease and subsequently a sharp increase at distances close to the core of the biofilm was observed.
source: For the velocity of the wavefront that travels back to the core, we observed a decrease and subsequently a sharp increase at distances close to the core of the biofilm (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: This unexpected behavior may be linked to the heterogeneity of microclusters within the bacterial biofilms.
source: This unexpected behavior may be linked to the heterogeneity of microclusters within the bacterial biofilms.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed velocity behavior.

claim: E. coli biofilms synchronize ion-channel-mediated electrical signaling when under external light stress.
source: E. coli biofilms synchronize ion-channel-mediated electrical signaling when under external light stress.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental data.

claim: The process of communicating the stress becomes faster as the intercellular distance decreases and it results in robust wavefront dynamics in which bacteria take turns to spike in a coordinated manner.
source: The process of communicating the stress becomes faster as the intercellular distance decreases and it results in robust wavefront dynamics in which bacteria take turns to spike in a coordinated manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of sparse cells, microclusters, and biofilms.

claim: Ion-channel-mediated wavefronts exist in 3D E. coli biofilms.
source: Our experimental data reveals that ion-channel-mediated wavefronts exist in 3D E. coli biofilms.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 3D confocal microscopy.

claim: 3D wavefronts exhibit anomalous diffusive behavior, which was well described by the 3D ABFDF model.
source: 3D wavefronts exhibit anomalous diffusive behavior, which was well described by our 3D ABFDF model.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of simulation and experimental data.

claim: The mode of propagation of the wavefronts was like that described for B. subtilis under nutrient stress.
source: The mode of propagation of the wavefronts was like that described for B. subtilis under nutrient stress (Prindle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work supported by a citation.

claim: Noticeable differences between E. coli and B. subtilis are in the frequency of oscillations, the latency, the dimensionality of the system, and the number of spikes (two hyperpolarization events with E. coli).
source: However, noticeable differences are in the frequency of oscillations, the latency, the dimensionality of the system, and the number of spikes (two hyperpolarization events with E. coli).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work on B. subtilis.

claim: Kch was the first potassium channel to experience detailed structural work in E. coli.
source: Although Kch was the first potassium channel to experience detailed structural work in E. coli Milkman, 1994, it has never been linked to membrane potential dynamics.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Milkman, 1994.

claim: Kch has never been linked to membrane potential dynamics prior to this study.
source: Although Kch was the first potassium channel to experience detailed structural work in E. coli Milkman, 1994, it has never been linked to membrane potential dynamics.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature prior to this study.

claim: The Kch channel plays an important role in E. coli membrane potential dynamics.
source: Our findings establish that the Kch channel plays an important role in E. coli membrane potential dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by the experimental data.

claim: The Kch channels control the refractoriness and second peak of the membrane potential.
source: Specifically, the channels control the refractoriness and second peak of the membrane potential.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Kch mutants.

claim: These phases of the dynamics were correlated with light stress modulation in E. coli biofilm.
source: These phases of the dynamics were correlated with light stress modulation in E. coli biofilm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Light-based E. coli biofilm treatments should be more effective if coupled with Kch targeting modalities.
source: We therefore predict that light-based E. coli biofilm treatments should be more effective if coupled with Kch targeting modalities.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the findings about Kch's role.

claim: Both the Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) model and the fire-diffuse-fire agent-based model provided new physical insights to understand photodynamic therapy.
source: Both of the two models developed, the Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) model and the fire-diffuse-fire agent-based model, provided new physical insights to understand photodynamic therapy.
evidence: This is a summary of the contribution of the models.

claim: The HH model satisfactorily describes the globally averaged dynamics of the membrane potential in response to blue light.
source: The HH model satisfactorily describes the globally averaged dynamics of the membrane potential in response to blue light and indicated a minimal model containing at least two ion channels (Q and Kch) was necessary to describe the double spiking response to blue light irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data.

claim: A minimal model containing at least two ion channels (Q and Kch) was necessary to describe the double spiking response to blue light irradiation.
source: The HH model satisfactorily describes the globally averaged dynamics of the membrane potential in response to blue light and indicated a minimal model containing at least two ion channels (Q and Kch) was necessary to describe the double spiking response to blue light irradiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling work.

claim: The fire-diffuse-fire agent-based model could quantify the anomalous dynamics of the wavefront and predicted the critical biofilm radius needed for wavefronts to propagate.
source: The fire-diffuse-fire agent-based model could quantify the anomalous dynamics of the wavefront and predicted the critical biofilm radius needed for wavefronts to propagate.
evidence: This is a summary of the capabilities of the agent-based model.

claim: Anomalous dynamics of wavefronts are not predicted by classical analytic solutions to reaction-diffusion equations.
source: Anomalous dynamics of wavefronts are not predicted by classical analytic solutions to reaction-diffusion equations and are thus a substantial advantage of the agent-based modeling approach we followed Keener and Sneyd, 2009.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and knowledge of reaction-diffusion theory.

claim: The unknown ion channel (Q) is not connected to calcium dynamics.
source: Our data shows that the unknown ion channel (Q) is not connected to calcium dynamics, but it is connected with the MS ion channels that work in tandem to propagate the initial spike in E. coli under light stress.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data with calcium sensors.

claim: The unknown ion channel (Q) is connected with the MS ion channels that work in tandem to propagate the initial spike in E. coli under light stress.
source: Our data shows that the unknown ion channel (Q) is not connected to calcium dynamics, but it is connected with the MS ion channels that work in tandem to propagate the initial spike in E. coli under light stress.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from MS channel mutants.

claim: Minimally the model predicts Q=MscK × MscL ×MscS, but the full dependence is probably more complex.
source: Minimally the model predicts Q=MscK × MscL ×MscS, but the full dependence is probably more complex.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model with acknowledgment of uncertainty.

claim: The initial spike is key to registering the presence of the light stress.
source: The initial spike is key to registering the presence of the light stress.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: When bacterial cells experience light-based stimulation, they experience stress which can be cytotoxic due to the production of ROS.
source: When bacterial cells experience light-based stimulation, they experience stress which can be cytotoxic (Wilson and Patterson, 2008; Abana et al., 2017) due to the production of ROS.
evidence: This is supported by citations about light-induced stress.

claim: The accumulation of ROS leads to deleterious oxidative stress that damages molecules.
source: The accumulation of ROS leads to deleterious oxidative stress that damages molecules (Wilson and Patterson, 2008; Mittler, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations about ROS effects.

claim: The propagation of action potentials in the presence of changing irradiance suggests that the stimulus strength is encoded in the response of the biofilms.
source: The propagation of action potentials in the presence of changing irradiance suggests that the stimulus strength is encoded in the response of the biofilms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the irradiance experiments.

claim: The membrane potential dynamics suggest a link between the duration of the stimulus, the oxidative stress due to the strength of the irradiance and the gating of the ion channels that modulate the dynamics.
source: The membrane potential dynamics also suggest a link between the duration of the stimulus, the oxidative stress due to the strength of the irradiance and the gating of the ion channels that modulate the dynamics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The unresponsive nature of E. coli after the second hyperpolarization event and its marked plateau voltage is reminiscent of the phenomenon of signal habituation in neurons.
source: The unresponsive nature of E. coli after the second hyperpolarization event and its marked plateau voltage is reminiscent of the phenomenon of signal habituation in neurons (Levitan and Kaczmarek, 2002).
evidence: This is a comparison with neuronal behavior supported by a citation.

claim: Neurons discriminate between external stimuli by observing a sustained decrement in response to a constant external stimulus.
source: Neurons discriminate between external stimuli by observing a sustained decrement in response to a constant external stimulus (Herman, 2013; Avery et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations about neuronal habituation.

claim: E. coli biofilms mostly switch to a viable, but non-culturable phenotype when exposed to either pulsed or constant blue-light therapy.
source: E. coli biofilms mostly switch to a viable, but non-culturable phenotype when exposed to either pulsed or constant blue-light therapy (Abana et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2018; Marasini et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations about blue light effects on E. coli.

claim: The habituation after light stress registration could be involved in the switch to a viable, but non-culturable phenotype.
source: We suggest that the habituation after light stress registration could be involved.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the observed habituation phenomenon.

claim: The ion-channel mediated long-range electrical membrane potential in E. coli biofilms help them to withstand light stress.
source: Our work shows that the ion-channel mediated long-range electrical membrane potential in E. coli biofilms help them to withstand light stress.
evidence: This is supported by the LiveDead assay results.

claim: The findings will provide a good framework for more detailed optogenetic studies of membrane potential signaling in E. coli biofilms and help inform photodynamic therapies to combat problematic biofilm infections.
source: We believe that our findings will provide a good framework for more detailed optogenetic studies of membrane potential signaling in E. coli biofilms and help inform photodynamic therapies to combat problematic biofilm infections.

source: Recent work indicates that waves of hyperpolarization also occur across biofilms of Neisseria gonorrhoeae Hennes et al., 2023; another example of electrophysiological phenomena in medically relevant biofilms.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hennes et al., 2023.

source: The signaling wavefronts were thought to be due to diffusion of ROS rather than the potassium ions observed with E. coli biofilms, but genetic experiments with ion channel mutants to clarify this issue were not performed.

source: The N. gonorrhoeae study used an analytic reaction-diffusion model to describe the signaling phenomena.

source: We have presented much better quantitative agreement of our model with the propagating wavefronts in E. coli biofilms using reaction-diffusion equations combined with agent-based modeling, for example the ABM FDF model is able to predict the anomalous dynamics of the wavefronts and the critical biofilm size for propagation of the wavefront.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current study's modeling approach with that of the N. gonorrhoeae study.

claim: Agent-based modeling should be applied to N. gonorrhoeae biofilms in the future due to the better handling of geometric constraints in the models.
source: Such agent-based modeling should be applied to N. gonorrhoeae biofilms in the future due to the better handling of geometric constraints in the models.

source: Connecting the membrane potential to photodynamic therapy implies that there will be synergistic effects of externally applied electric fields and blue light on bacterial infections.
